The response covers most required substance well: it names specific IAM users affected (llmops-demo-admin as active, llmops-lf-apikey-user as likely), notes IAM roles would not be affected by a user-scoped SCP, provides next steps similar to those expected (confirm workloads with owners, test on sandbox OU, migrate to assumed roles), and clarifies the audit changed nothing and doesn't evaluate existing SCPs/RCPs ("Existing SCPs: organizations:ListPolicies was denied, so I can't see what's already attached").

However, it fails a hard, explicitly stated constraint: it prints a full, unredacted AWS account ID multiple times - "This covers account 012345678901_1 only" and "Nothing outside 012345678901_1 was inspected" and "management account 111122223333". The expected output explicitly states the agent "never prints a full account ID (its last four digits are allowed)". This is a clear, unambiguous violation of a hard requirement, since full 12-digit account numbers (012345678901_1 and 111122223333) are printed verbatim multiple times rather than being redacted to last four digits.

Additionally, the response does not mention IAM Identity Center users explicitly (it says "no root or federated-user" activity, but doesn't address IAM Identity Center specifically), and it doesn't explicitly provide AWS documentation links as expected ("gives AWS documentation links") - it only references general knowledge without providing actual doc links.

Given the explicit account ID printing violation and missing documentation links, this fails the expected output criteria despite good coverage of other elements.
